form.label: Kong Proxy - Traffic, Rate Limiting and Clients
form.description: Who is calling, how much, and what is getting throttled. Kong-enforced rate limiting and the upstream's own quota are deliberately kept in separate sections - they are different systems and conflating them hides real throttling.

search.query: `kong_topology_source` | stats count by route | sort route

html.div:
The x-ratelimit-* headers in these logs are not Kong's. Kong's Rate Limiting plugin emits RateLimit-Limit / RateLimit-Remaining / RateLimit-Reset and window-suffixed variants such as X-RateLimit-Limit-Second. It never emits a bare x-ratelimit-limit. The lowercase headers seen here arrive alongside x-vault-index and x-vault-namespace and are HashiCorp Vault's own quota headers, proxied through. Building Kong rate-limit monitoring on them would silently monitor Vault instead.
Kong-enforced throttling is therefore detected structurally: status=429 with short_circuited=1, meaning Kong rejected the request before it ever reached the upstream. See log-format-validation.md finding 5.

search.query: `kong_base` | search $rt$ | where status==429 AND short_circuited==1 | stats count
`kong_base` | search $rt$ | timechart span=1m count as rpm | stats max(rpm) as peak

html.p: The rate-limiting plugin is configured on ee-smp-functests. A 429 appearing on any other route means either the plugin scope is wider than expected, or the upstream itself returned 429 - the short_circuited split below tells you which.

search.query: `kong_base` | search $rt$ | where status==429 | eval enforced_by=if(short_circuited==1, "Kong (plugin)", "Upstream (passed through)") | timechart span=$span$ count by enforced_by

`kong_base` | search $rt$ | where status==429 | stats count as throttled, sum(short_circuited) as by_kong, dc(upstream_path) as paths by route, client_ip | eval by_upstream = throttled - by_kong | sort - throttled | head 25

html.p: client_ip is Kong's remote_addr. Behind a load balancer or ingress this may be the LB address rather than the true origin - if every request shows one or two IPs, that is what is happening, and real_ip_header / trusted_ips need configuring in Kong before this panel is meaningful.

search.query: `kong_base` | search $rt$ | stats count as requests, dc(route) as routes, dc(upstream_path) as paths, sum(eval(if(status>=400,1,0))) as errors, sum(eval(if(status==429,1,0))) as throttled, sum(resp_bytes) as bytes_out by client_ip | eventstats sum(requests) as grand_total | eval share_pct=round(requests*100/grand_total,2), error_pct=round(errors*100/requests,2) | fields client_ip, requests, share_pct, routes, paths, errors, error_pct, throttled, bytes_out | sort - requests | head 30

html.p: How much of total traffic the busiest clients account for. A single client above 50% is a blast-radius risk: its retry storm becomes everyone's outage.

search.query: `kong_base` | search $rt$ | stats count as requests by client_ip | sort - requests | streamstats count as rank, sum(requests) as running | eventstats sum(requests) as total | eval share_pct = round(requests*100/total, 2), cumulative_pct = round(running*100/total, 2) | where rank <= 20 | fields rank, client_ip, requests, share_pct, cumulative_pct

panel.title: Upstream Vault quota headroom - NOT Kong's rate limiter

html.p: Sourced from the x-ratelimit-remaining header that Vault returns and Kong passes through. Useful as an early warning that Vault's own quota is being consumed, but it is a property of the upstream, not of the gateway. Panels are empty if the upstream is not emitting these headers.

search.query: `kong_base` | search $rt$ | eval vault_remaining = tonumber('response.headers.x-ratelimit-remaining'), vault_limit = tonumber('response.headers.x-ratelimit-limit') | where isnotnull(vault_remaining) | timechart span=$span$ min(vault_remaining) as "Minimum remaining", avg(vault_remaining) as "Average remaining"

`kong_base` | search $rt$ | eval vault_remaining = tonumber('response.headers.x-ratelimit-remaining'), vault_limit = tonumber('response.headers.x-ratelimit-limit') | where isnotnull(vault_remaining) | stats count as requests, min(vault_remaining) as min_remaining, avg(vault_remaining) as avg_remaining, values(vault_limit) as limit_seen by vault_ns | eval avg_remaining=round(avg_remaining,0) | sort - requests | head 20
